content.text:
Short version: on the numbers, auto-add can't survive v2 as it is.

- **The model**: 81.0% of spines read correctly (1,004 of 1,240 photos, 96 shelves). Ravi's own threshold for auto-add is 95%.
- **Where it misses**: tilted spines 34%, glare 27%, thin spines 21%, stacked or sideways books 12%, other 6% of the 236 wrong reads. Confidence doesn't separate right from wrong well, so a threshold on it won't fix this.
- **The PRD today**: Requirements say nothing is added until the steward taps "Add", but Open question Q1 still asks whether to keep auto-add for stewards whose scans are 95%+ accurate.
- **Caveat**: the glare set is only 140 photos from 9 shelves, so treat the glare share as soft.

I'd leave Q1 open until we have the beta evidence next to the eval. Want me to check the two against each other?

Here's Denise's email and her screenshot from the Linden Street box. This is why auto-add has to wait.

Hi Sam,

Thanks for asking, here's everything in one go because I've been meaning to write it down.

I look after the Linden Street box, the one with the glass door (Gerald says it's the fanciest in the beta, I say it just has a good lock). I usually scan around 4pm when I do my rounds, and that's exactly when the sun comes round the corner and hits the glass. The app just gives up. It takes the photo, then half the spines come out as nonsense and I can't tell until later.

Last week it added "Pervasive Games: A Handbook" to my shelf. The book was Persuasion! I know because I put it there myself. I didn't notice until Mrs. Abernathy from number 14 walked all the way over for it, in the drizzle, and she was very nice about it but I felt dreadful.

Honestly I stopped scanning for a few days after that. It isn't that I mind the app being wrong sometimes, glass is glass. It's that it put the wrong book in without asking me.

If the app asked me first, "is this Persuasion?", I would happily check each book. I'd rather tap ten times than have Mrs. Abernathy come over for nothing. I think a lot of stewards would say the same.

Also, small thing, it would be lovely if it warned me about the glare before I took the photo. I'd just open the door.

I attached a screenshot of the wrong match so you can see it.

Thanks for listening, and good luck with the next version!

Denise (Linden St box)

# Shelf scan v2: PRD

Sam · Oct 13, 2026 · for the team review on Thu Oct 15

## Problem
Shelf scan reads about four spines in five correctly, and v1 adds every spine it reads to the catalog. So one book in five on a scanned shelf is wrong. Neighbours walk to a box for a book that isn't there, and stewards stop trusting the scan.

## Goals
1. **Fewer than 3% wrong books** in the catalog (19% today).
2. 80% of scans end with a saved shelf (64% today).
3. A steward reviews a 14-book shelf in under 20 seconds.

## What we heard
Three of eight testers (P3, P6, P8) stopped scanning after a wrong book was added for them.
Glare from glass-door boxes caused 27% of wrong reads; Denise (P3) can't scan her box at all after 4pm.
With a [review step](../prototype/scan-review.html) in the prototype, testers fixed every miss: 97% of books right, median 18 s a shelf.
Owen (P8) stopped after two wrong books in two scans.

## Requirements
After a scan, show every spine found on the photo, and flag the ones the model is unsure of.
Fixing a flagged book takes one tap: pick from the top three matches, or type the title.
Nothing is added to the catalog until the steward taps "Add".
Warn about glare before the photo is taken, and suggest opening the door.

## Non-goals
1. A new spine-recognition model; Ravi's model work runs separately.
2. Scanning by neighbours who aren't the box's steward.

## Open questions
Q1. Auto-add: keep it for stewards whose scans are 95%+ accurate, or remove it until the model reaches 95%?
Q2. Do we keep v1's wrong books, or ask stewards to re-scan?
- Do stewards want the glare warning before every scan, or only at glass-door boxes?
